info.title: Wardrik daemon
info.description: The daemon's own routes, beside Wardrik's operations (see Wardrik's openapi.json, at /v1/openapi.json). Each takes the same bearer tokens, and is decided by config.yaml's roles and bindings: x-wardrik-action is what a caller must be allowed to do, on the resource x-wardrik-resource names. Tokens are in no org, so only a binding in * reaches them. An owner is one path segment: acme for an org, acme%2F%40jon for a person, or deployment. A resource the caller reaches none of is answered as one that doesn't exist.

get.description: The names of the secrets the owner holds, and what each is for, including the accounts they connected. Never a value.

put.description: Seals the value as the owner's secret of that name, in place of any it held, and reconnects the owner's MCP servers whose headers read it. The deployment's are what ${NAME} in config.yaml reads.

delete.description: Removes the owner's secret of that name. Removing none answers as removing one does.

get.description: Each budget the org's policies pool, with what its agents have spent against it in its period now.

get.summary: List the MCP servers an owner's agents reach
get.description: The owner's own, then those it gets from further out: a person's org's, then the deployment's, including those config.yaml gives the owner's org. Each says which owner holds it. The nearest of a name wins, as the agents see it.

post.summary: Add an MCP server for an owner's agents
post.description: An org's server serves its own agents and every agent of its people; a person's serves their agents alone. It starts on every node, and its tools reach the agents from their next turn. The URL must pass the deployment's egress check.

201.description: That its agents can call it now, or where someone signs in to it first.

delete.description: One of the owner's own. It stops on every node, its tools leave its agents from their next turn, and the sign-ins to it are forgotten.

get.summary: List the notify targets an owner's agents route to
get.description: The owner's own, then those it gets from further out: a person's org's, then the deployment's, including those config.yaml gives the owner's org. The nearest of a name wins. Each says which owner holds it.

post.summary: Add a webhook for an owner's agents' notices
post.description: An org's target serves its own agents and every agent of its people; a person's serves their agents alone. One of the owner's own by the same name is a conflict; one held further out is overridden. The URL must pass the deployment's egress check.

201.description: The notify target, as it's kept.

delete.description: Only the owner's own. Agents routing to it find the next one out by the same name, if there's one.

200.description: The notify target, as it was.

get.description: Every token, by ID, never its secret.

post.description: A token that acts as its subject, with its groups, until it expires. Its secret is answered this once: only its hash is kept. The resource is the subject, so a rule's names can say which subjects a caller may make tokens for. A token for user:admin is the admin's alone to make, whatever the caller's bindings.

delete.description: It stops working at once. Revoking none answers as revoking one does.

owner.name: owner
owner.description: The owner, as acme for an org, acme%2F%40jon for a person, or deployment.

Unauthorized.description: No token, or one that isn't known or has expired: unauthorized.

Forbidden.description: The caller reaches the resource, but may not do this to it: forbidden.

NotFound.description: There's no such resource, or the caller reaches none of it: not_found.

Conflict.description: It has one of that name already: conflict.

secrets.title: An owner's secrets
secrets.description: Each secret the owner holds, by name, and what it's for. Never a value.

purpose.description: What it's for: api_key, client_secret, header or signing_secret for one the owner sealed, grant for an account they connected, token for a chat app's install, secret for one sealed with no purpose.

secret_input.title: A secret to seal
secret_input.description: The value to seal, and what it's for. A secret is read only for its purpose, so a client secret is never read as an API key.

purpose.description: api_key for a key code calls a service with, client_secret for an OAuth app's, header for an MCP server's header, signing_secret for a webhook's.

ceilings.title: Ceilings
ceilings.description: Each of an org's ceilings, with what its agents have spent against it in its period now.

per.description: How long its limit lasts before it starts over.

on_exhausted.description: What the org's next model call does once they've spent it: waits on a ceiling_approval, is refused, or runs.

starts_over.description: The day it starts over, in its timezone. Absent for a ceiling in total.

server_input.title: A server to add
server_input.description: What servers.add takes: the server's name, its URL, how the owner's agents sign in to it, and which of its tools they take.

name.description: What the owner's agents call it: their definitions name its tools as name/*, and each tool arrives as name__tool. Letters, digits, - and _, up to 32, never __.

url.description: The server's whole URL, over https, reached as Streamable HTTP.

auth.description: How the owner's agents sign in to it.

oauth.description: The owner signs in in a browser, and the token is kept for them. Left bare, the server's own authorization server is found from its URL, and the daemon becomes its client itself. Where it can't be, as with a service that publishes no metadata or registers no clients, name an OAuth app the owner can use as provider, or give the app they registered there: its issuer or its endpoints, its client_id, and the name of the secret they keep its client secret under.

scopes.description: The scopes to ask for, the server's own unless it says.

issuer.description: The authorization server's issuer URL, whose metadata names its endpoints.

authorization_endpoint.description: Where a person signs in, where the issuer publishes no metadata. Given with token_endpoint.

token_endpoint.description: Where a code is exchanged for a token. Given with authorization_endpoint.

client_id.description: The owner's OAuth app's client ID.

client_secret.description: The app's client secret, as a secret the owner keeps in the vault. It's read each time it's needed, so a new value takes effect at once, and never sent anywhere but the token endpoint.

name.description: The secret's name in the owner's vault.

client_auth.description: How the client secret is sent: in the form, or as HTTP Basic. post unless it says.

authorization_params.description: Extra parameters for a browser sign-in, as access_type: offline. Can't set the ones the daemon sends itself.

provider.description: An OAuth app to sign in with, by name: the owner's, their org's or the deployment's. Takes the place of an app given here.

secret.description: A key the owner keeps in the vault, sent with every call.

name.description: The secret's name in the owner's vault.

header.description: The header it is sent in; authorization unless it says.

scheme.description: What comes before it in the header; Bearer unless it says, and nothing where it is empty.

only.description: The server's own names of the tools to take, every one unless it says.

except.description: The server's own names of the tools to leave.

server_added.title: A server added
server_added.description: What servers.add answers: that the owner's agents can call the server now, or where someone signs in to it first.

connected.description: Whether its agents can call it now.

authorization.description: Where to sign in to it, where someone has to first.

server.title: An MCP server
server.description: An MCP server an owner's agents reach: who holds it, where it came from, its URL, and how its agents sign in to it. Never its headers.

name.description: What the owner's agents call it.

url.description: The server's URL. Omitted for a command the deployment starts.

auth.description: How its agents sign in to it.

servers.title: MCP servers
servers.description: What servers.list answers: the MCP servers an owner's agents reach, their own and those they get from further out.

notify_target_input.title: A notify target to add
notify_target_input.description: What notify_targets.add takes: a webhook the owner's agents' notices are posted to, and the secret that signs them.

name.description: What agents' definitions route to, as notify: ops. Letters, digits, - and _, up to 32.

url.description: Where notices are posted, over https. Checked as it's added and as each notice is sent, and never followed through a redirect.

secret.description: Signs each notice's body, as a secret the owner keeps in the vault. It's read as each notice is sent, so a new value takes effect at once.

name.description: The secret's name in the owner's vault.

notify_target.title: A notify target
notify_target.description: A place an owner's agents' notices go: who holds it, where it came from, and what kind it is. Never its secret, nor a config target's options.

kind.description: What sends its notices, as webhook or room. A target added at runtime is a webhook.

url.description: Where a webhook posts. Omitted for other kinds.

secret.description: The vault secret that signs a runtime webhook's notices. Omitted for one without, and for a config target.

name.description: The secret's name in the owner's vault.

notify_targets.title: Notify targets
notify_targets.description: The targets an owner's agents' notices go to: their own, and those they get from further out, the nearest of a name winning.

token_input.title: A token to create
token_input.description: Who the token acts as, and for how long. The caller needs a binding on the token kind.

name.description: What it's for, to tell tokens apart.

subject.description: Who it acts as: user:ID, or agent:ID for an agent's own.

groups.description: The groups a user: token's principal is in, which bindings may name.

expires_in.description: Seconds until it stops working: at least a minute, at most a year. 30 days unless set.

token.title: A token
token.description: A token the HTTP API is reached with. Never its secret.

id.description: The token's ID, which revokes it.

token_created.title: A token created
token_created.description: The token, with its secret. The secret is shown this once: only its hash is kept.

id.description: The token's ID, which revokes it.

secret.description: Send it as Authorization: Bearer. Shown once.

amount.description: An amount in dollars, tokens or both. A limit leaves out what it doesn't limit.
